questions.question: In story S22 (Delete superseded modules and drop the forks), is there any vacuous or placeholder production path: a no-op/stub body, a tautological assertion, a frozen stand-in constant, or an optional dependency (injected port, handler, client handle) that silently degrades to non-behavior when not injected? Cite file:line for each injection point in app/src/lib/marmot/* (listed deletions); app/package.json + lockfile (make deps); app/next.config.mjs (keeps ts-mls include); remaining importers of deleted modules and show that omitting the dependency fails loudly rather than succeeding silently.

Could `MarmotContext` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md (imports only via each module's index.ts, no React-context imports under app/src/lib/marmot/**, no ts-mls or @internet-privacy/marmot-ts imports)?

Does S22 comply with the architecture.md boundary rules: only `client/` constructs or disposes the MarmotClient, code inside HistoryBackend calls / inbox handlers / client listeners never awaits an account-scope client call (follow-up work via the owned setTimeout(0) FIFO), group sender identity comes only from orderingKey.account, and idb-keyval update() is not used? List each rule touched by this story's files with file:line evidence, or state why it is not touched.

Do unit, property, and (where the AC names them) library-harness or e2e tests cover the artifacts named in S22's scope (app/src/lib/marmot/* (listed deletions); app/package.json + lockfile (make deps); app/next.config.mjs (keeps ts-mls include); remaining importers of deleted modules)? Show that tests use real collaborators or test fixtures rather than mocking the helper used at the SUT call site, that idb mocks are seeded out of key order where order matters, and that at least one test fails if the production code is replaced by a no-op.

Does the delivered S22 implementation match the intent of its scope (Delete NdkNetworkAdapter, welcomeSubscription, epochResolver, rumorJournal, applicationRumorDispatcher, keyPackages, state/key-package backends in groupStorage, pendingRemovalStorage, leftGroupTombstones, staleLocalGroup, staleReplaceMarker, replaceTeardown, membersChangedSync, inviteeKeyPackageLook) and respect its exclusions (Storage keys/stores grep and dead exports (S23))? Identify any capability owned by a later story that was built ahead, or any in-scope capability left unimplemented.

Which trust or validation boundaries does S22 touch (signer budget/permissions, relay-supplied events, rumor sender/pubkey attribution, invite/join payloads, privacy invariant that no profile metadata is published to public relays)? Show the validation or defensive check at each boundary with file:line evidence and a test that feeds a malformed or hostile input and observes rejection.

AC-DEP-2: `app/package.json` MUST NOT list `@internet-privacy/marmot-ts` or `ts-mls` as dependencies. `@hpke/*` and `@noble/post-quantum` MUST be absent unless a grep of `app/src` and `app/tests` finds a remaining import of them. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [structural] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies. Because the AC is structural, show the verification command's output on the pre-change tree and on the post-change tree and confirm they differ.
